text:
ella (Support): FYI just got an escalation from AcmeCorp — they see p95 ~450ms and p99 ~1.25s for /v1/complete in eu-west for the last 90m. They also reported intermittent 401s during high latency windows. Ticket SVC-8273.
rohit (eng-sre): timeline? is this sudden or gradual? any deploys or infra changes?
ella (Support): Customer says spike started ~1782101500 (about 45m ago). No deploys on their side. Our monitoring shows a TTL increase in request latency to eu-west region around 1782101400.
sam (eng-infra): I'm pulling edge route changes. No rollout in eu-west within that window. However, our infra autoscaler did a scale-up of dedicated pools at 1782101200, might have bumped routing.
jin (eng-runtime): Are we seeing an auth backend latency bump too? If token validation is added to the critical path that could account for 200-300ms.
ella (Support): Support-bot logs attached in the ticket show auth latencies oscillating between 50ms and 400ms. Some of the 401s coincide with the higher auth latencies.
rohit (eng-sre): Can someone paste a traceroute and a TLS log from eu-west edge for a failing request? Need to see cross-AZ hops.
sam (eng-infra): Ran traceroute from one impacted edge instance to customer IP via our load balancer. Paste below:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.12.1.1 (10.12.1.1)  0.512 ms  0.492 ms  0.480 ms
 2  10.12.200.1 (10.12.200.1)  1.5 ms  1.4 ms  1.4 ms
 3  edge-nat-eu-west-azc (10.20.3.5)  10.2 ms  10.0 ms  9.9 ms
 4  core-router-2 (192.0.2.9)  23.4 ms  23.6 ms  24.1 ms
 5  isp-peering-3 (198.51.100.2)  24.0 ms  24.1 ms  24.2 ms
```
sam (eng-infra): Notably we see two cross-AZ hops before exiting; our latency baseline usually shows 1-2ms inside AZ, not 9-10ms at hop 3.
rohit (eng-sre): That suggests traffic is being hairpinned across AZs. Any BGP or routing changes?
sam (eng-infra): There was an emergency BGP session reset with one of the peering routers at 1782101300 due to announce flapping; the route-flap mitigator flipped a next-hop to a standby path which takes a different AZ egress.
jin (eng-runtime): TLS logs from the edge during spike: auth handshake RTTs: 90ms normal -> 320ms during spike. Also seeing increased resend of ClientHello? Not exactly, but a longer time to complete 0-RTT fallback.
rohit (eng-sre): So combined effect: cross-AZ egress adds ~8-12ms, extra packets and a BGP reroute add jitter, auth backend timeouts add 200-300ms, total pushes p99 up. 401s could be from auth timeouts or token cache misses.
maria (product): Is any customer traffic routed to eu-central fallback? We need to consider traffic segregation for Dedicated customers.
ella (Support): AcmeCorp is on Hosted (shared) and also has a Reserved Dedicated shard for some models. They reported both hosted and dedicated traffic impacted.
linda (cust-success): Their logs show retries from their SDK increasing. They hit billing thresholds because of retries; customer is upset.
rohit (eng-sre): Quick mitigations: 1) Pin traffic to same-AZ egress where possible (route attribute change) 2) Bump auth backend timeouts and add extra replicas + warm token cache 3) Enable region-fallback policy to eu-central for non-auth-critical calls 4) Ask customer to increase client timeout briefly to reduce retries.
sam (eng-infra): I can push a route attribute to prefer local egress on affected edge nodes. Rolling that out now to eu-west-azc and eu-west-azb edge pools. Will monitor.
jin (eng-runtime): I'll scale auth validators x2 and increase internal token cache TTL from 60s -> 180s for now. Also enable sticky connection reuse for edge -> auth to reduce handshake overhead.
rohit (eng-sre): Also let's add a temporary firewall rule that prevents unhealthy NAT gateway from being used as next-hop. If route-flap mitigator picks it again we need a quick kill switch.
sam (eng-infra): Route update applied to azc and azb pools at 1782103500. Pushed a BGP dampening tweak to reduce next-hop flips.
ops-bot: Route update event applied by sam at 1782103500. Monitoring set: p99 latency eu-west edges.
rohit (eng-sre): Any immediate signal improvement?
sam (eng-infra): Early numbers: p95 dropped from 450ms -> 260ms within 90s of the change; p99 now ~610ms down from 1.25s. Auth error rate (401) decreased by 70%.
ella (Support): Customer confirms partial improvement, still seeing occasional spikes every ~7-10m.
jin (eng-runtime): Those residual spikes look like occasional backend GC pauses on one auth replica. Scaling should help; I'm looking at GC logs. Also rolling a JVM flag to shorten full GC.
rohit (eng-sre): For next steps: 1) sam to keep route preference in place and confirm BGP stability for 2h 2) jin to finish auth scaling + GC tuning and revert token-cache TTL after 24h 3) maria/linda to coordinate a customer communication and credit for extra retries 4) i'll run a deeper packet capture during next spike window.
sam (eng-infra): I'll keep the mitigations for 4 hours at least and will post an update if BGP dampening misfires.
jin (eng-runtime): Auth replicas scaled and GC flags applied at 1782103800. Token cache TTL set to 180s temporarily.
linda (cust-success): Drafting a note to AcmeCorp summarizing what we did and offering a billing credit for retry impact. Will share in 30m.
rohit (eng-sre): After 60m of observation p99 stabilized ~350-420ms. Recommend we keep fixes until end of day and then do a controlled rollback: revert token TTL and keep route preference if stable.
ella (Support): I'll update the ticket SVC-8273 and let the customer know we're monitoring. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
maria (product): Long term: put guardrails in the route-flap mitigation so it avoids cross-AZ egress unless absolutely necessary. Also add auth latency SLO alarms tied to routing changes.
rohit (eng-sre): Agree. I'll create a follow-up runbook item: "Edge routing flap -> verify same-AZ egress -> scale auth -> apply token-cache TTL" and link to incident timeline.
ops-bot: Runbook created by rohit: RB-1149 at 1782104600.
rohit (eng-sre): Closing thread for now. If any regression, ping me directly @rohit and I'll re-open.
